newsitem.title: USA: Kansas board asked to drop Nigeria investments.
newsitem.headline: Kansas board asked to drop Nigeria investments.

text.p: Trustees of the Kansas Public Employees Retirement System (KPERS) were set Friday to consider a request to rid the state pension fund of its investments in companies doing business in Nigeria.
The advocacy group Bias Busters of Kansas has asked the board to divest holdings in Royal Dutch/Shell group, Mobil Corp and Chevron Corp.
The group's leader, Sonny Scroggins, said those companies were helping prop up a system that has been criticized for human rights violations.
Scott Peppard, assistant investment officer for KPERS, said KPERS assets at the end of July totalled $6.7 billion.
Peppard said that as of earlier this week, KPERS holdings in the three targeted companies had a market value of $54 million.

When asked if there was any indication of how the trustees would vote, Peppard said, "There is some legislation in place that was passed back in 1992 that prohibits (the trustees) from making decisions based on anything other than economic considerations."
